The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Namavarapu Rajeshwar Rao

Judgment:

entities.text:
Shakuntala Bai And Another vs Depot Manager And
Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This MACMA is filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 by the appellants/petitioners aggrieved by the order and decree dated 25.02.2013, passed in M.V.O.P.No.2339 of 2011 by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-Cum-Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad (for short "the Tribunal").

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-Cum-Chief Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. For the sake of convenience, the parties will be hereinafter referred to as they are arrayed before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that the petitioners filed a claim petition under Section 163(A) of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- on account of the death of Bharathi Bai (hereinafter referred to as "deceased") stating that on 26.03.2012 while the deceased was aged 26 years and was hale and healthy prior to the accident.
She used to work as a maidservant and earn Rs.5,000/- per month.
It is stated that the petitioners are the parents of the deceased, and on 21.08.2011, the deceased along with her mother went to Ameerpet for shopping.
After completing the 2 RRN,J shopping, they were proceeding towards Bus stop to go to their residence.

While so, at about 12.30 hours when they reached near Adithya Enclave, one APSRTC Bus bearing No.AP-11Z- 7406 was driven by its driver at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the deceased.
As a result, the deceased fell down and had sustained a head injury and died on the spot.
On a report, the police, S.R. Nagar Police Station, had registered a case in Cr.No.803 of 2011 under Section 304- A IPC against the driver of the said RTC bus.
4. Respondents filed counter denying the petition allegations.
5. To prove their case, petitioners examined PW.1 and got marked Exs.A1 to A5.
On behalf of respondents, neither oral nor documentary evidence was adduced.

6. On appreciation of the evidence on record, the Tribunal allowed the O.P. in part by awarding compensation of Rs.4,23,000/- with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Challenging the same, the present appeal is filed by the petitioners.

7. Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners inter- alia contended that the Tribunal erred in considering the 3 RRN,J monthly income of the deceased at Rs.3,000/- per month, and he relied upon the judgment reported in 2012 ACJ 1428 in the case of Santhoshi Devi Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd., wherein the Hon'ble Supreme Court was pleased to consider Rs.5,000/- per month Smt.Shakuntala Bai And Another vs Depot Manager And Another on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165836761/
1 towards the services rendered by a housewife, apart from her earnings.

entities.text: Santhoshi Devi Vs. National Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Shakuntala Bai And Another vs Depot Manager And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further contended that the Tribunal did not grant compensation amount under the conventional heads.
Hence, prayed to allow the appeal.

He also placed reliance on the judgment rendered by this Court in M.A.C.M.A.
No.2719 of 2015 wherein this Court considered the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month as the deceased apart from housewife, was doing tailoring business.
8. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for respondents contended that the Tribunal was justified in passing the impugned order, which calls for no interference by this Court.
Accordingly, prayed to dismiss the appeal.
9. Heard both sides.
Perused the record.

10. Having considered the rival contentions of both parties, this Court is of the considered view that the Tribunal had granted compensation in terms of II Schedule (Section 163-A) prevailing at that time considering the age of the 4 RRN,J deceased as 26 years.

The learned counsel for the petitioners contends that the Tribunal had considered the meagre monthly income of the deceased at Rs.3,000/- per month and the same is to be enhanced in view of the judgments referred above.
This Court in M.A.C.M.A. No. 2719 of 2015 considered the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month as the deceased apart from housewife, was doing a tailoring business.
But, in the case on hand, the petitioners failed to adduce any evidence that the deceased was earning something apart from housewife.
Considering the judgment relied upon by the learned counsel for petitioners in the case of Santhoshi Devi (Supra), this Court is inclined to fix the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.5,000/-.
To this, future prospects of 40% as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi1 as the deceased was aged 26 years.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The annual income of the deceased including future prospects would come to Rs.84,000/- (Rs.5,000/- + 40% x 12).
The appropriate multiplier as per the decision of Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation2 is "17".

entities.text: Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Since the deceased was a bachelor, a deduction of 50% of the income towards personal expenses which the (2017) 16 SCC 680.
(2009) 6 SCC 121.
5 RRN,J deceased might have spent for herself

. Thus, the total loss of dependency would come to Rs.7,14,000/- (Rs.84,000/- - 50% x 17).
11.
The Tribunal awarded Rs.5,000/- funeral expenses, Rs.5,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.5,000/- towards transportation.

However, the petitioners are entitled to compensation under conventional heads as per the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs Pranay Sethi and others3and Magma Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Nanu Ram @ Chuhru Ram4 towards loss of filial consortium to each petitioner Rs.40,000/- i.e. Rs.80,000/- (i.e.
Rs.40,000/- x 2); Rs.16,500/- towards funeral expenses and Rs.16,500/- towards loss of estate.
12.

sentences.text: In the result, the M.A.C.M.A is allowed and the compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced from Rs.4,23,000/- to Rs.8,27,000/- (Rupees Eight Lakh and Twenty seven Thousand only)

with interest @7.5 % p.a. from (2017) 16 SCC 680.
42018 Law Suit (SC) 904 6 RRN,J the date of petition till the date of realization.

Respondents No.1 and 2 are directed to deposit the said amount with costs and interest after deducting the amount, if any, already deposited, within two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

On such deposit, the petitioners are permitted to withdraw the same in accordance with the manner and proportion as determined by the Tribunal subject to payment of deficit Court fee within two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions, if any pending, shall stand closed.
